proof_layers.name: content_exists
proof_layers.description: File contains meaningful Kingsmen content, not an empty placeholder.

proof_layers.name: manifest_consistency
proof_layers.description: Structured manifest records the doctrine, tool, provider, package, source-confidence, or module state.

proof_layers.name: validator_exists
proof_layers.description: A validator script exists for the module or batch.

proof_layers.name: validator_passed
proof_layers.description: Validator exits successfully and does not hide failures.

proof_layers.name: report_written
proof_layers.description: Validator writes an honest JSON report with passed true/false, checked files, missing files, and next action.

proof_layers.name: git_checkpoint
proof_layers.description: Changes are committed to Git/GitHub with traceable commit history.

proof_layers.name: ui_api_proof
proof_layers.description: UI/API surfaces load or respond where applicable.

proof_layers.name: runtime_proof
proof_layers.description: Local Docker or runtime command proves the module can run.

proof_layers.name: oracle_staging_proof
proof_layers.description: Oracle Lite staging proves the module can operate under constrained deployment rules.

hard_rules: No production-ready claim without runtime and staging proof.
No UI claim without clickable or route proof.
No current source claim without source confidence evidence.
No package access gating of core Kingsmen gates.
No raw secrets in repository files.
No OpenClaw raw-secret or production-write access by default.
No fake guarantee of acceptance, funding, job, accommodation, or success.
No mock/random analytics as production truth.
